ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6774 of Dec. 31, 2002, last amended by Act No. 19477 of Jun. 10, 2023; Presidential Decree No. 33233 of Dec. 29, 2022); Act on Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (Act No. 15246 of Jan. 1, 2018); Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Secrecy Act (Act No. 15192 of Nov. 1, 2017); Guidance of the Financial Services Commission and Financial Intelligence Unit on Customer Due Diligence (FSC/FIU Notice No. 2023-2). The implementation of beneficial-owner identification is governed by Articles 5 and 9 of the Reporting Act and its Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 31822, May 12, 2021).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office (competent corporate registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Notarization (waived because the certificate is issued directly by the court registry); Step 2: Apostille certificate issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea under the Hague Apostille Convention. For destination states not party to the Apostille Convention, obtain consular legalization exclusively from the destination state's diplomatic mission in Korea; never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Corporate Registration Detailed Certificate, 법인등기사항 전부증명서)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent District Court Registry (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Notarization not required for this court-certified document; Step 2: Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (Hague Apostille). If the receiving state is not an Apostille Convention member, use only a Korean consular/seal-legalization issued by that state's embassy in Seoul; no sequential hybridisation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution authorising incorporation and appointment of the initial Representative Director (including Power of Attorney, if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Board of Incorporators / Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Notarization by a Korean notary public; Step 2: Apostille certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (Hague Apostille). For non-Hague destination states, consular legalization by the destination state's consulate in Korea is substituted for the Apostille; the two authentication methods remain parallel and exclusive, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (정관, final executed version)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators; register-filed copy available from the District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Notarization of all incorporators' signatures by a Korean notary public; Step 2: Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Apostille Convention). If the target state is a non-member of the Hague Convention, consular legalization must be obtained instead from the competent consular office of that state in Korea; never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming account opening and completed Customer Due Diligence (UBO) review
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank (e.g., KEB Hana Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank, KB Kookmin Bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Notarization by a Korean notary public (if the bank letter is not on bank seal paper); Step 2: Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea under the Hague Apostille Convention, unless the receiving jurisdiction is a non-member, in which case the sole path is consular legalization via that jurisdiction's embassy/consulate in Korea. Apostille and consular legalisation are mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Subject individuals and entities must be screened against (i) the consolidated list of the Republic of Korea's Financial Actions against North Korea and Global Terrorism (Korea's consolidated sanctions list issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the Act on Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism); (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List and UN sanctions resolutions; (iii) the US OFAC SDN List and OFAC sectoral/non-SDN lists; (iv) the EU consolidated sanctions list; and (v) law-enforcement databases of PEPs, at least (a) on-boarding, (b) real-time transaction monitoring, and (c) 24-hour re-checks upon any change in beneficial ownership. Any hit requires Escalation Review by the AML Compliance Officer and a Suspicious Transaction Report to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KFIU) within 3 business days if the transaction triggers reporting under Article 4 of the Reporting Act. PEP status includes domestic and foreign prominent public officials, their family members and close associates; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for such clients. Automated screening must cover fuzzy-matching logic, ID-number variations, and jurisdiction-specific name transliterations, and all results must be retained for 5 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO) – https://www.iros.go.kr (also accessible via the corporate registry of the competent District Court)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Article 24 of the Commercial Act and the Commercial Registration Rules, the statutory corporate name (상호) must be stated in the Korean alphabetic script (Hangul) and may simultaneously be registered as a foreign-language trade name in English or another alphabet. Transliteration of foreign words into Hangul must follow the Revised Romanization of Korean (Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism Notice No. 2014-42) and the National Institute of Korean Language's foreign-word orthography. The name must maintain the four-tier naming structure: (1) a distinctive trade name; (2) an object-descriptive term identifying the enterprise's principal business; (3) the legal-form suffix 주식회사 (Chusik Hoesa) or, where applicable, 유한회사; and (4) any geographic designation which, if included, must accurately reflect the principal place of business and may not create confusion with a government authority or another enterprise.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed name (e.g., for likelihood of confusion with an existing company or violation of Article 23 of the Commercial Act), the incorporator must first file a written objection with the Registry Office that rendered the decision within 14 days of receipt of the rejection notice. The registry will re-examine and issue a signed decision. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may, within 90 days of the renewed decision, institute an administrative appeal before the competent Administrative Court under the Administrative Litigation Act (Act No. 3754, as amended). As a strategic fallback, the law firm must simultaneously prepare a revised name combination reflecting the registry's stated objections and may request re-use of the applicant's original priority date if a corrected application is filed within 7 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: South Korea's Commercial Act and Commercial Registration Rules require a definite and identifiable registered office (본점) for tax registration and service of process. A so-called virtual office or commercial mailbox address may be accepted at the registration stage if the address belongs to an approved office-sharing/registered-agent facility and a valid lease is submitted. However, Korean banks (especially for corporate account opening) and the National Tax Service (NTS) will typically reject or heavily scrutinise a pure virtual mailbox without physical office equipment, employees or actual business activity; the NTS may impose a business-site verification that requires a physical meeting at the registered address. For a MarTech SaaS company with no office staff in Korea, a virtual address is permissible only if there is a compliant local agent, a real sub-lease and adequate substance obligations are assumed, otherwise account application and tax registration are likely to be denied.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood of an unannounced NTS or municipal inspection in the first 12 months is MODERATE–LOW (approximately 30% for new software/IT companies with a foreign shareholder and no payroll). Checklist used by inspectors: (i) verifiable signage at the registered office; (ii) employment records and social insurance filings for at least one resident employee; (iii) business-related power, telecommunication and internet invoices; (iv) corporate seals and original certificates physically available; (v) up-to-date VAT bookkeeping; and (vi) consistency between the business scope and actual web-server usage/contracts. Embedded continuous audit trail of server logs and cloud subscriptions is strongly recommended.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 288-330 (incorporation of stock companies), Article 289 (articles of incorporation), and Article 292 (registration of incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the Local District Court (under the Supreme Court of Korea)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and Application for Incorporation Registration (법인설립등기신청서)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act. The company must issue at least one share and the full subscription price must be paid into a corporate bank account before registration. No escrow account requirement is imposed by law, but the paid-in capital must be verifiable via bank deposit certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (CHUSIK HOESA)

Pursuant to the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and the Articles of Incorporation of the Company, the first meeting of the Board of Directors was duly convened and held on [Date] at [Time] at the registered office of the Company. All Directors were present, and the meeting was conducted in accordance with applicable law.

WHEREAS, the Company has been incorporated for the purpose of conducting information technology and software services, including search engine optimization data analytics, keyword research, and related digital marketing tools;

NOW, THEREFORE, the Board of Directors hereby resolves as follows:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board confirms that the total authorized share capital of the Company is [Amount] KRW, divided into [Number] shares of [Par Value] KRW each. The initial paid-up capital of [Amount] KRW has been fully subscribed and paid by the shareholders as per the subscription statements. The Board ratifies the issuance of shares to the initial shareholders and authorizes the preparation and delivery of share certificates accordingly.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts with [Bank Name] and any other financial institution as deemed necessary. The Board appoints the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer as the authorized signatories for all banking transactions, with the power to sign, endorse, and withdraw any documents related to the Company's accounts. The Board further authorizes the use of online payment processing services, including Stripe and Paddle, for the collection of revenues from the Company's software-as-a-service offerings.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [Address], Republic of Korea, as the official legal address for all corporate communications, statutory notices, and service of process. The Board authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to execute any lease or service agreements necessary for the maintenance of such office and to file any required changes with the relevant authorities.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board hereby appoints the following officers to serve in their respective capacities: [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary. Each officer shall have the authority and responsibilities as prescribed by law and the Articles of Incorporation. The Board further appoints [Name] as the statutory auditor, if required under the Commercial Act, to oversee the Company's financial affairs.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes the officers to take all necessary actions, execute all necessary documents, and make all filings required to complete the foregoing resolutions, including but not limited to the registration of the Company with the Commercial Registration Court, tax authorities, and any other regulatory bodies.

This resolution is effective immediately and shall be recorded in the minutes of this meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Court (online portal) and Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Commercial Registration Court's online system to ensure the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing registered entities. Reserve the name for a period of 30 days. Simultaneously, perform a trademark search with KIPO to avoid infringement. Verify the legal capacity of all proposed directors and shareholders, ensuring no disqualifications under the Commercial Act. Prepare a preliminary list of shareholders, directors, and officers, and confirm the registered office address is available for lease or ownership.
required_dossiers: List of shareholders with shareholding amounts
Identification documents of directors and officers
Proof of address for registered office (lease agreement or title deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an alternative name within 14 days or appeal the decision to the court. If trademark conflict arises, modify the name or obtain a consent letter from the trademark holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the company name, business purpose, registered office address, authorized share capital, number of shares, and provisions for directors and auditors. The articles must be signed by all incorporators and notarized by a licensed notary public. The notary will verify the identity of the incorporators and the legality of the articles. After notarization, the articles become the founding document of the Company. Ensure all statutory requirements under Articles 289-292 of the Commercial Act are met.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, correct the articles and re-submit for notarization. If the notary refuses, seek a different notary or obtain a court order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription and Payment of Shares, and Appointment of Directors and Auditors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's internal process (documented for court filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the full subscription amount from each shareholder into a temporary bank account opened in the Company's name. Obtain a bank deposit certificate as proof of payment. After payment, convene a general meeting of incorporators to appoint the initial directors and auditor (if required). The directors then hold a board meeting to appoint the CEO, CFO, and other officers. Prepare minutes of both meetings, signed by all participants. Ensure all appointments comply with the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Bank deposit certificate or proof of payment
Minutes of the general meeting of incorporators
Consent forms from each director and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is not made, the incorporation process is suspended. If any director is disqualified, replace them and re-convene the meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Commercial Registration Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Court (local district court) – online e-registration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for incorporation registration with the court, attaching the notarized Articles of Incorporation, proof of payment, minutes of meetings, and identification documents. The court will review the application for compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the court issues a Certificate of Incorporation, and the Company is legally established. The registration must be completed within 14 days of notarization of the articles. After registration, obtain a corporate seal certificate and register for tax identification with the National Tax Service.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of shares (bank certificate)
Minutes of general and board meetings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court queries the application, respond to the query within 7 days. If rejected, correct the defects and re-file. If the 14-day deadline is missed, the notarized articles become void and the process must restart.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr); customs clearance portal: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (https://unipass.customs.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestically incorporated Chusik Hoesa, legal incorporation is effected with the Korean court registry, after which the company must file a Business Registration Application with the competent district tax office via HomeTax or in person. On successful filing, NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as the unified corporate tax identification number and VAT registration number. A foreign non-resident entity that has no domestic place of business but must register for Korean corporate income tax or VAT activity must appoint a Korean tax representative and file the Business Registration Application at the district tax office with jurisdiction over the tax representative's address, attaching the foreign certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, board resolution appointing the tax representative, power of attorney, and any required due diligence certificates. NTS then issues a foreign corporation business registration number which is used for all corporate tax, withholding tax, VAT, and e-invoice reporting obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or a general hybrid entity classification election. A Chusik Hoesa is treated as a domestic corporation under the Commercial Act and is subject to entity-level corporate taxation; no pass-through eligibility is available for equity shareholders.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary registration threshold. Any business operator engaged in taxable supplies in Korea must complete VAT business registration before commencing activities, irrespective of forecast turnover. A simplified taxpayer category applies to certain individual businesses with annual VAT-exclusive revenue not exceeding 80,000,000 KRW, but simplified status does not remove the mandatory registration obligation or the obligation to file periodic VAT returns.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax e-invoice system for qualifying supplies, and the issuer must transmit the e-invoice to NTS no later than the day following the supply. System-to-system transmission via the HomeTax open API is supported for ERP integration. The NTS maintains third-party reconciliation and risk-matching analytics on e-invoice data; there is no physical fiscal stamp, but the e-invoice is validated and stored by NTS. Electronic tax invoices must be retained for a minimum of five years and reconciled with VAT return declarations; failure to transmit or systematic under-reporting triggers administrative penalties and audit action.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the Korean VAT Act applies to exported goods which are physically shipped from Korea to a foreign territory and accompanied by customs export clearance. It also applies to qualifying offshore services supplied to non-residents, including cross-border digital content, software, SEO analytics, and similar electronically supplied services where the recipient is a foreign purchaser and the service is deemed supplied outside Korea under the statutory foreign-payment and foreign-consumption criteria. To sustain 0% VAT, the Korean supplier must obtain and retain contemporaneous proof of actual delivery or service performance, full commercial documentation, and documentary evidence that the export consideration is paid from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Customs Declaration (Bill of Entry) issued through UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical movement of goods out of Korea (not applicable for offshore digital services)
Commercial invoice and signed export/offshore service contract

Foreign exchange purchase/remittance certificate or inward remittance certificate (payment receipt certificate) proving that the consideration was received in a foreign currency from the overseas customer
Service performance documentation for digital services, including server or usage logs and customer acceptance records where available
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service may jointly review export zero-rating claims, refund applications, and electronic tax invoice records. If the supporting export or offshore service evidence is missing, forged, non-contemporaneous, or inconsistent, the NTS may deny the 0% rate and assess undeclared VAT at the standard 10% rate together with interest and penalties. Fraudulent or abusive refund claims may attract an additional penalty surcharge of up to 40% of the refunded or underpaid VAT amount, and deliberate tax-fraud cases may be referred to the prosecutor's office under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Additionally, failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days or materially inconsistent foreign exchange documentation can trigger both VAT clawback and foreign exchange regulatory sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a broadly convertible foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is freely convertible for current-account transactions, including cross-border SaaS subscription fees, royalties, and service charges, provided each settlement is handled through a licensed foreign exchange business bank and the underlying economic purpose is documented. The capital account is partially controlled: foreign direct investment into a Chusik Hoesa, the acquisition of shares, and the remittance of paid-in capital require the mandatory filing of a foreign exchange transaction report through the receiving bank, and certain large or unusually structured capital flows may require ex-ante regulatory review. Exporters are no longer subject to a hard surrender quota; they may retain foreign currency proceeds in approved foreign currency accounts. For dividend distributions, the bank requires audited financial statements, a board resolution declaring dividends, corporate tax payment or waiver confirmation, and a Form 17-style foreign exchange declaration. In practice, banks also enforce FATF/Korea Financial Intelligence Unit beneficial ownership rules and may independently ask for underlying documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from regulated goods and services must be collected and received into a licensed domestic foreign exchange account within 180 days of the export declaration or the contractual due date for intangible digital services, whichever is applicable; longer collection periods for multi-year or project-type digital service contracts require an approved extension through the bank and the relevant Korean trade insurance authority. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0%; there is no fixed export surrender obligation to the Korean won, but receipts must be reported to the domestic foreign exchange bank and the company must retain the export service contract, customer invoice, and payment confirmation for at least five years as part of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act compliance file.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for foreign direct investment; Basic Operational Currency Account in KRW and foreign currency
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account with trade settlement sub-limits
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account; foreign currency demand deposit for export proceeds
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account; foreign currency corporate settlement account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Very Low and legally non-viable for treasury account purposes. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, or Mercury are not licensed as Korean foreign exchange business banks under the Banking Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; therefore they cannot hold a Korean corporate account, cannot accept a paid-in capital contribution for capital verification, cannot satisfy the statutory foreign exchange declaration and tax clearance requirements, and cannot underpin dividend repatriation. Stripe and Paddle may be used only as merchant-of-record rails for customer card collection, with the net settlements remitted to the Korean treasury account at a domestic tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A face-to-face compliance interview is mandatory for foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa account openings at tier-1 Korean banks. The statutory representative director must appear in person at a domestic branch and produce a valid passport or Alien Registration Certificate; a pure remote consular-proxy account opening is not generally accepted. If the sole director is abroad, the practical alternative is to appoint a Korean resident director or grant a notarised power of attorney to a local officer, but the Korean bank will still require the authorised person to appear and present proof of appointment, board resolution, and the company seal/legal registry extraction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No operating history and a business model that relies entirely on foreign payment aggregators, making the Korean entity look like a shell or sleeping company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised articles of incorporation, Korean business registration certificate, board resolution for account opening, audited or management-prepared proforma financial statements, executed SaaS/SEO content analytics customer contracts, customer traffic and payment gateway settlement statements, registered office lease and staff engagement records, and a narrative treasury plan showing expected inbound and outbound settlement flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder sends a large paid-in-capital remittance from a personal account or from a jurisdiction with less transparent corporate registers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Equity subscription agreement and board/shareholder resolutions, certified corporate register of the shareholder, ultimate beneficial ownership chart to natural persons, passport copies of all UBOs, tax residence certificates, bank statements of the remitting account, source-of-wealth evidence such as dividends, salary, property sale contracts, or a certificate of loan balance, and a signed AML questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name or date-of-birth match on sanctions, PEP, or adverse media screening lists, or negative news from the marketing jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full individual KYC records including passport bio-data page and current taxi/home address, independent sanctions and PEP screening report with no verified match, official corporate registry extract of the Korean entity, a Korean counsel legal opinion on the ultimate ownership and control chain, an explanation letter from the UBO, and where necessary an official police clearance or regulatory good-standing certificate from the home jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital is verified in the bank but the company has no current corporate tax reporting or dividend-relevant income, and the bank requests assurance that the entity is a genuine cross-border service exporter
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FDI notification/receipt issued by the receiving bank, capital verification certificate from a Korean certified public accountant, current corporate tax return or confirmation of filing, VAT/withholding tax certificates, service export contracts, invoices for each customer, proof of payment received through Stripe/Paddle, and a detailed cash-flow projection covering working capital and future dividend remittance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injection must be settled by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's licensed bank to the Korean entity's foreign currency demand deposit account at a domestic authorized foreign exchange bank. The wire must identify the beneficiary as the Chusik Hoesa, include the business registration number and the receiving bank SWIFT BIC, and state the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose code for acquisition of equity securities in Field 70, with the memorandum Capital Contribution to KR_CHUSIKHOESA. Upon receipt, the bank issues a foreign exchange purchase/capital contribution confirmation; the company must file the inward foreign investment report through the bank within 30 days, and a certified public accountant must verify the paid-in capital before the balance is transferred to the KRW operational account. All original remittance advices and the FDI notification must remain in the treasury compliance file for subsequent dividend and capital verification reviews.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for trade settlements for this SEO content analytics business is SWIFT MT103 for licence fees, search-engine data subscriptions, analytics platform fees, royalties, and cloud infrastructure disbursements. The Korean entity must issue proper export invoices and retain service-level agreements so the bank can match the outbound payment to the underlying export declaration. Commercial letters of credit may be used only when the software analytics product is bundled with physical appliances or servers; the software component is then invoiced separately and settled via MT103. Documentary collections are acceptable for a limited set of long-standing counterparties, but the bank will require a full copy of the contract and payment terms to ensure the transaction is not being used to shift value offshore.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts through a Korean tier-1 bank for genuine commercial exposure, limited to forecast receivables and payables evidenced by invoices or purchase orders
Cross-currency swaps with a licensed Korean bank for existing or projected trade-related liability, subject to board approval and BOK reporting requirements

Non-deliverable forwards may be accessed only with prior regulatory approval and only for non-resident counterparties or exceptional risk management cases; speculative offshore KRW NDFs are not permissible for a domestic Korean treasury.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and approval of the financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing; minutes kept at the registered office; Commercial Registry Court filing only if the articles are amended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be judicially ordered to convene a meeting and may face an administrative fine under Commercial Act Article 635 of up to KRW 10,000,000; no automatic strike-off, but repeated non-compliance can support a court petition for judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months from fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, due 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing triggers a 20% additional tax on the unpaid tax, an under-reporting surcharge of 10% or 40% for fraudulent returns, and daily overdue interest of 0.022% until full payment; prolonged delinquency can result in seizure of corporate assets, business registration cancellation, and a creditor or NTS petition for court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the corporate income tax filing deadline; for a calendar-year company, due 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts a 20% additional tax on the assessed local tax, plus daily overdue interest of 0.03%; local authorities may impose compulsory collection and auction corporate property; persistent non-filing can support cancellation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Four annual submissions: 25 April for January-March, 25 July for January-June, 25 October for April-September, and 25 January for July-December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing attracts a 20% additional tax of the unpaid VAT; delayed payment accrues daily overdue interest at 0.022%; failure to issue valid tax invoices triggers a 2% penalty on supply value; two consecutive periods of failure to file permits NTS to deregister the VAT business status, effectively blocking SaaS invoicing and triggering forced tax assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage and salary income tax employer statement and monthly withholding returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual employment income statement due by 10 March for the preceding calendar year; monthly withholding returns due by the 10th of each following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delayed submission incurs a withholding penalty of 0.5% per month up to 20%; unpaid withheld taxes attract a 20% surcharge and 0.022% daily interest; continued non-payment can lead to asset seizure and criminal prosecution for willful evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Company annual management report, where a non-resident shareholding qualifies under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, due 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted FIPA reports can lead to loss of foreign-invested-company status, withdrawal of tax treaty and incentive benefits, and an administrative fine of up to KRW 3,000,000; false reporting may trigger heavier FIPA penalties and enforcement action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report and audited financial statements filing, applicable only when the statutory audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before the annual shareholders' meeting; the auditor must file the report with FSS no later than 2 weeks after the audit report date, practically before 31 March for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violation of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies can subject the company and directors to fines of up to KRW 100,000,000 for audit obstruction, FSS mandatory auditor designation, disciplinary orders, and regulatory enforcement; this does not trigger administrative strike-off but constitutes a serious statutory non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, mandatory independent CPA audit applies to: (i) all stock companies listed on a Korean securities exchange, irrespective of size; and (ii) unlisted stock corporations, including a Chusik Hoesa, whose total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000. For ordinary unlisted Chusik Hoesa, turnover and headcount do not independently trigger the audit obligation; however, an audit may also be required where shareholders holding at least 3% of issued shares request it, where a financial authority or court mandates it, or where the Financial Services Commission designates the company as a public-interest entity. If the company forms part of a consolidated group under K-IFRS, group consolidated assets equal to or above the same statutory threshold also trigger a group audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed and certain large unlisted companies; Korean Accounting Standards / K-GAAP (Non-Public Enterprise Accounting Standards) for ordinary non-listed Chusik Hoesa; all statutory audits are performed in accordance with the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Korean Standards on Auditing; Corporate Tax Act book-tax reconciliation records are maintained in parallel with financial-statement books.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not maintain a public beneficial-ownership register for private Chusik Hoesa. The company must keep its shareholder register current and update it immediately upon each share transfer; a transferee is opposable to the company only after registration in that register. Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, any qualifying non-resident acquisition of at least KRW 100,000,000 and 10% or more of shares must be reported to MOTIE through KOTRA within 30 days of the transaction, and subsequent foreign share transfers, pledges, or capital changes must also be reported within 30 days. Consequently, there is no annual UBO confirmation filing; the operative UBO obligation is the transactional 30-day reporting window plus ongoing AML/KYC disclosure to Korean financial institutions when the company opens or maintains bank accounts or payment rails.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Auditors
Register of Stock Pledges and Beneficial Interests in Scripless Shares
Minute Book of Board of Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,200 per annum for a registered office address and corporate secretarial agent in Seoul, excluding e-filing and bookkeeping
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - 12,000 per engagement for a small-to-mid-sized unlisted SaaS analytics company with simple capital structure; USD 12,000 - 30,000 for a K-IFRS consolidated statutory audit.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% national corporate income tax on the taxable-income slice above KRW 300 billion; aggregate top marginal effective rate 27.5% after adding the 10% local income tax surcharge.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested high-tech businesses, including digital content and SaaS activities, may qualify for 100% corporate income tax exemption for 5 years and 50% exemption for the following 2 years under foreign investment promotion provisions. The Special Tax Treatment Control Act also provides R&D expenditure tax credits, employment-creation credits, venture/start-up preferential rates, and favorable depreciation for software capital expenditure.
